definition: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique for large language models and other deep neural networks.
details: Introduced in 2021 by researchers at Microsoft, LoRA enables adaptation of pre-trained models to specific tasks while requiring significantly fewer computational resources and trainable parameters than traditional full model fine-tuning.
story: Think of a grammar teacher who never memorized a rule but can still tell you when a sentence sounds wrong. In plain words: LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique for large language models and other deep neural networks. Here is how it actually plays out: Introduced in 2021 by researchers at Microsoft, LoRA enables adaptation of pre-trained models to specific tasks while requiring significantly fewer computational resources and trainable parameters than traditional full model fine-tuning. The machine learns to read between the lines by reading an impossible number of lines. That pattern-earned fluency is LoRA (machine learning).
